name: Startup MVP
tagline: The smallest stack that can serve real users and still be refactored later
summary: One deployable application, one relational database, a managed host and a CDN. Nothing here is chosen because it scales to millions; everything is chosen because a small team can ship, debug and change it quickly.
basis: TechFlow archetype, not a specific company's stack. It reflects the defaults we would pick for a new product with one to five engineers and no proven traffic.

items.note: One UI framework the whole team already knows.
Types pay for themselves the first time you rename a field.
Static assets and cacheable pages served near the user.
Same language as the client; the ecosystem covers most integrations.
Clear internal modules, one deployment. Split later only if you must.
Boring, cacheable, easy to debug with curl.
Relational by default; JSONB covers the parts you have not modelled yet.
Two good indexes beat any cache you have not needed yet.
Server sessions are simpler to revoke than tokens at this size.
Social login avoids owning password reset flows on day one.

items.label: Managed platform (PaaS)
items.note: Someone else runs the machines until that stops being the bottleneck.
Push to main, tests run, deploy. Nothing manual.
Reproducible builds even when the host abstracts them away.

items.label: Hosted error tracking
items.note: You need the stack trace before you need dashboards.
Structured logs from the first commit; metrics when there is traffic to measure.

whenToUse: Fewer than about five engineers and no validated traffic pattern
The product shape is still changing weekly
You would rather pay for managed services than run infrastructure
Correctness and iteration speed matter more than cost per request
tradeoffs: A single deployable means one bad release affects everything
Managed platforms cost more per unit of compute than raw servers
No cache and no queue means every slow dependency is felt by the user
You will outgrow parts of this — plan for the seams, not for the rewrite
